text:
devon: Quick sync — we need a concrete benchmarking protocol for the next perf pass. goal: apples-to-apples comparison across kernels, batching heuristics, and quant profiles. thinking replay harness + targeted synthetic. thoughts?

maria: +1 on replay harness for realistic KV/cache patterns. but we should keep a synthetic Poisson/steady mix too to stress batching. :thinking:

sam: agree. can we define the exact metrics up front? P50/P95/P99 lat, tokens/sec, cost-per-token, and regression delta vs baseline. also memory/GPU utilization.

oliver: For apples-to-apples we must freeze: model weights, tokenizer, seed traces, and env (cuda/driver). otherwise kernel differences become noisy.

maria: suggestion: run three arms per experiment: 1) replay (100% production traces, KV warm states), 2) synthetic steady (constant arrival rate matching mean QPS), 3) spike mix (bursts to validate routing/fallback). compare same sample set across kernels.

devon: sounds good. add a warmup protocol: 30s priming with same trace to populate KV cache and steady batching before measuring. without warmup numbers are worthless.

sam: important callout: kernel selection experiments must be deterministic. we should pin kernel versions and run each arm twice (A/B) to rule out jitter. include seed for RNG in speculative decoding.

qa-liz: test harness note: replay_harness currently replays at original timestamps which can underutilize GPUs for small traces. propose replay_harness --rate-scale to multiply inter-arrival times so we can get sustained throughput. also add --kv-warmup-file to prepopulate cache.

devon: good — example command for clarity:
```
replay_harness \
  --trace s3://prod/traces/2026-02-28.json \
  --rate-scale 2.0 \
  --kv-warmup-file s3://prod/kv_warm/2026-02-28.seed \
  --target-model rwd-llama-13b-quant 
```

maria: let's record kernel-level counters and per-kernel timeline from the runtime profiler (nvtx + our perf collector). we need per-op breakdown (matmuls, softmax, kv-fetch) to map regressions.

sam: on quant profiles — please include at least: fp16 baseline, 8-bit symmetric, 4-bit grouped, and one mixed-precision with selective attention in fp16. measure both output quality (perplexity on eval set + a small prompt-based QA pass) and perf.

oliver: speculative decoding: measure happy-path latency reduction and the frequency of correction tokens (where speculative path is rolled back). log mismatch rate and cost overhead of rollbacks. quality tradeoff: does speculative increase repeat tokens or hallucinations? capture via a small prompt suite.

qa-liz: regression gate proposal: automated gate fails CI if throughput drops >5% at P95 or branch increases mismatch rate for speculative >1.5x. manual triage if cost reduction >10% but quality delta borderline.

devon: agree on gate thresholds as a starting point. we'll iterate. who owns the benchmark run orchestration?

maria: I'll own the automation for the replay + synthetic arms and collect artifacts. sam take profiler integration. qa-liz own the quality eval harness. oliver will run kernel pinning and config matrix.

sam: one more: canonicalize sequence-length distribution for synthetic tests. we'll run short (<=64), medium(128-256), long(512+) buckets separately so batching behavior is clear.

oliver: logging detail: include per-request kv-hit bool, batch-size at time-of-service, and kernel-name/version. those are the keys to correlate perf with cache behavior.

qa-liz: add a post-run sanity check that compares token distributions and attempts to detect sampling variance in replay vs synthetic. flag runs with >3% distribution shift.

devon: timeline: run baseline (fp16, current kernels) tomorrow, then 4-bit and speculative next week. results in shared perf dashboard, and we'll post a regression/merge decision doc.

maria: note for dashboards — include cost-per-token and an adjusted metric 'effective latency' that includes rollback penalty for speculative.

sam: cc perf-bot — please schedule nightly runs for the matrix and post aggregated artifacts to /perf/artifacts/<run_ts> so we can compare automatically.

perf-bot: Scheduled nightly run 1792185600 for matrix: [rwd-llama-13b:{fp16,8bit,4bit}, speculative:{on,off}] - artifacts will appear in /perf/artifacts/1792185600. :robot_face:

oliver: thanks. small follow-up: when we compare kernels, also run with kernel-threshold overrides (force older kernel) to validate selector logic. sometimes selector defaults to a perf-favoring kernel but has a correctness penalty.

devon: agreed — add a 'selector-forced' column in results. okay team, let's keep runs minimal but deterministic. ping me in thread with links to artifacts. :thumbsup:
